children: Goobit Group AB (“Goobit” or “the Company”) has published its interim report for the first quarter of the financial year 2026/2027, available at goobit.se. The quarter was weaker than the corresponding period last year, mainly due to the absence of OTC transactions. After the end of the period, the Company changed how its exchange business is conducted, which affects how revenue is recognised from the second quarter onwards. The Company encourages everyone to read the full report.
Overview of financial results
Q1, 1 MAY 2026 TO 31 JULY 2026
COMPARED WITH THE CORRESPONDING PERIOD LAST YEAR
Net sales amounted to SEK 19.9 million (23.3).
Gross profit amounted to SEK 0.8 million (3.1), corresponding to a gross margin of 4.0 per cent (13.5).
EBITDA amounted to SEK -2.0 million (-0.9).
Operating profit amounted to SEK -2.8 million (-1.7).
Profit for the period amounted to SEK -2.9 million (-1.9).
Earnings per share before and after dilution amounted to SEK -0.01 (-0.01).
Cash and crypto assets amounted to SEK 8.6 million (12.3) at the end of the period.
Transaction volume amounted to SEK 19.9 million (29.4). The group carried out no OTC transactions during the period.
Significant events during the period

On 11 May, XXI Capital AB assumed an existing loan of SEK 5.5 million from Blockchain AB to Goobit Group AB. The refinanced loan carries no interest, runs for five years and may be repaid early. At maturity, Goobit may repay 50 per cent in cash and 50 per cent in shares at market value, and XXI Capital AB may use the claim for set-off in a future share issue.

On 2 July, the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority rejected Goobit AB’s application for authorisation as a crypto-asset service provider under MiCA. The Company requested reconsideration and appealed the decision on 23 July, objecting that the authority had not made a sufficiently individual and proportionate assessment and that the Company had not been given reasonable time to answer material questions. The Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority rejected the request for reconsideration on 28 July, and the matter is now before the Administrative Court in Stockholm. In connection with the process, Goobit AB strengthened its independent control functions with full-time roles as Chief Compliance Officer, Money Laundering Reporting Officer and Risk Manager.
Significant events after the period

In August, the remaining parts of the exchange business were changed from trading against the Company’s own bitcoin inventory to the execution of customer orders. As the Company no longer takes a position in the underlying asset, revenue from these transactions is recognised net from the second quarter of 2026/2027. The accounting policies are unchanged and comparative figures are not restated. Applied to the first quarter, revenue of SEK 19.9 million and exchange costs of SEK -17.9 million would have been recognised as approximately SEK 2.0 million with exchange costs of SEK 0.2 million, with gross profit unchanged. Reported revenue and gross margin for the second quarter will therefore not be comparable with the first quarter, and transaction volume will continue to be reported alongside revenue.

On 14 August, it was announced that Gustav Buder succeeds Christian Ander as Chief Executive Officer with effect from 15 August 2026. Christian Ander continues in a more strategic role on the Company’s board.

On 31 August, the extraordinary general meeting elected Joakim Dahl as a new board member for the period until the end of the next annual general meeting. Carl-Viggo Östlund left the board with immediate effect.
On 2 September, the Company sold 3 BTC from its bitcoin treasury for SEK 2,216,674 to finance its ongoing operations. After the sale, the holding amounted to 8.34 BTC.
For further information, please contact:
Gustav Buder, CEO, Goobit Group AB
E-mail: ir@goobit.se
About Goobit Group

Goobit Group AB (publ) operates in the financial sector and is the parent company of BTCX, which offers bitcoin-focused services. The group consists of the wholly owned subsidiaries Goobit AB and Goobit Blocktech AB and is headquartered in Stockholm.
For more information, visit www.goobit.se
